About

| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **51.4.16** | [ADDED] Verify that if the authorization server supports unauthenticated dynamic client registration, it mitigates the risk of malicious client applications. It must validate client metadata such as any registered URIs, ensure the user's consent and warn the user before processing an authorization request with an untrusted client application. | 3 |

I would keep it a L2 requirement, probably even L1. In this scenario, I think the the risk of abuse by a malicious application is high.

We are in a scenario where anyone can register a client application on the AS.

If we we don't enforce user consent verification, any malicious website can:

1. register itself as an OAuth client on the AS,
2. when you visit the malicious website, start an OAuth flow;
3. obtain an access token on your behalf without your user consent;
4. use the protected APIs on your behalf.

This is an "open-bar" authorization server.

Follow-up of PR #2648
